Kopytka:

  • 2 cups cooked, mashed potatoes
  • 2 large eggs
  • 1 1/2 cups flour
  • 2 tablespoons oil
  • Dash of baking powder
  • 1 large spoonful of butter/margerine
  • Garlic cloves - as many as you want
  • Salt, pepper, any other seasoning you want

Prep:

  • Boil the potatoes until soft and mashable. You may leave the peel on, as long as it can be mashed well. Puree the garlic cloves. Season with a few dashes of salt and pepper, and about one garlic clove worth of the puree. Mash all ingredients except the remaining garlic and butter together by hand, until thick like dough. Should be quite sticky. Roll into small, oval dumplings. I usually do about an inch wide and an inch and a half long.

Cooking:

  • Boil water and add a splash of oil. Boil dumplings until they float to the surface. Drain water, and mix around in the pot with the large spoonful of butter, which should also stop them from sticking. In a small container, take remaining garlic puree and add salt and water to form a thick, garlicy paste. Drizzle garlic mixture over kopytka and enjoy.
